hunks.baseline: Looking back, I think I’d wondered about death from the time I was very young.
hunks.sol: Looking back, I think I’d wondered about death since I was very young.

hunks.baseline: That didn’t mean I was particularly precocious, of course.
hunks.sol: Not that I was particularly precocious.

hunks.baseline: Why was the amusement park I’d been promised a trip to if I got a perfect score on my spelling test blazing on the TV screen?
hunks.sol: Why was the amusement park I’d been promised a trip to if I got a perfect score on my spelling test burning on TV?

hunks.baseline: Why was there a pure white bouquet on the desk of the classmate who’d played with me just yesterday?
hunks.sol: Why was there a white bouquet on the desk of the classmate I’d played with just yesterday?

hunks.baseline: That was all. It was just the kind of era we lived in.
hunks.sol: That was simply the age we lived in.

hunks.baseline: An age of chaos, where truths so vast and terrible that nothing could stop them kept spilling out without end.
hunks.sol: An age of chaos, with truths too vast and terrible for anyone to hold back spilling out without end.

hunks.baseline: I quickly came to understand what it meant when my parents changed the TV channel with grim faces, and what the pure white bouquet on my friend’s desk meant.
hunks.sol: I soon understood why my parents had changed the TV channel with grim faces, and what the white bouquet on my friend’s desk meant.

hunks.baseline: But my kindergarten teacher’s choice to call my friend’s absence a “long journey” left me with even more questions.
hunks.sol: But my kindergarten teacher’s description of my friend’s absence as a “long journey” left me with even more questions.

hunks.baseline: That it was a grown-up’s way of showing consideration didn’t change the fact that one thought led to another, then another.
hunks.sol: I understood that she’d been trying to be kind. Still, one thought led to another.

hunks.baseline: Where do they go after they die?
hunks.sol: Where do they go when they die?

hunks.baseline: If they really have gone on a journey, does a world beyond death truly exist?
hunks.sol: If they really do go on a journey, is there a world beyond death?

hunks.baseline: Even after a long time had passed, there was no one who could answer those questions for me.
hunks.sol: Even after many years, no one could answer those questions for me.

hunks.baseline: Of course there wasn’t.
hunks.sol: Of course they couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: So I wanted to find the answer from someone who had died, but wasn’t dead anymore.
hunks.sol: So I tried asking someone who had died but wasn’t dead anymore.

hunks.baseline: “……Why did you call me? Get to the point.”
hunks.sol: “…Why did you call me? Get to the point.”

hunks.baseline: I’d secretly believed that Bones—or rather, the Skeleton King—could answer the question that had haunted me for so long.
hunks.sol: Deep down, I’d believed Bones—or rather, the Skeleton King—could answer the question I’d carried for so long.

hunks.baseline: But faith was often betrayed.
hunks.sol: But faith has a way of being betrayed.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. I don’t know a thing. I don’t remember my life before death, so why would what came after be any different? I just woke up in the dark like this.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. I don’t know a thing. I can’t remember my life before I died, so why would I know any more about what came after? I just woke up in the dark and found myself like this.”

hunks.baseline: Even an undead being who had already crossed death’s threshold and been reborn didn’t know what lay beyond it.
hunks.sol: Even an undead being who had risen from death knew nothing about what lay beyond it.

hunks.baseline: In the end, I gave up on finding an answer.
hunks.sol: In the end, I gave up looking for an answer.

hunks.baseline: Or, more precisely, I put it off.
hunks.sol: Or rather, I put it off.

hunks.baseline: I’d learn someday.
hunks.sol: I’d find out someday.

hunks.baseline: Whether I wanted to or not, that thing called death would hide in the shadows, biding its time, then swallow everything whole.
hunks.sol: Whether I wanted to or not, death would wait in the shadows for its moment, then swallow everything whole.

hunks.baseline: Just—
hunks.sol: Just like now.

hunks.baseline: Like this very moment.
Ssshhh.
hunks.sol: *Ssshhh.*

hunks.baseline: The wails they poured out, the shouts of battle that still hadn’t faded.
hunks.sol: Their cries, and the shouts still rising from the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: The past I’d struggled through. Fleeting moments I’d let slip by without a thought.
hunks.sol: The past I’d struggled through. The fleeting moments I’d let slip away.

hunks.baseline: With no voice left to escape my lips, I sank weakly.
hunks.sol: No sound came from my lips as I sank helplessly.

hunks.baseline: Into the swamp of death, pulling hard at my soul.
hunks.sol: Into the swamp of death, tugging hard at my soul.

hunks.baseline: And in a gap in time that felt like eternity, I heard someone’s voice echo as if in a hallucination.
hunks.sol: And in a gap in time that felt like eternity, I heard a voice echo as if in a hallucination.

hunks.baseline: Whooosh!
hunks.sol: *Whoosh!*

hunks.baseline: A beam of light appeared from nowhere, somehow, tearing through the darkness and illuminating the world.
hunks.sol: A beam of light appeared from nowhere, tearing through the darkness and illuminating the world.

hunks.baseline: I blinked blankly.
hunks.sol: I blinked, dazed.

hunks.baseline: Then, looking at the sight spread out before me, I wondered:
hunks.sol: Then I took in the sight before me and wondered:

hunks.baseline: It was a vast space—or no, so boundless that even “vast” didn’t begin to describe it. An expanse of grayish white stretched without end.
hunks.sol: The gray-white space stretched on without end. Even “vast” felt too small a word for it.

hunks.baseline: The horizon, drawn far in the distance, was hazy. When I looked up, there was a ceiling overhead, higher and more distant than the sky.
hunks.sol: The horizon far in the distance was hazy. When I looked up, I saw a ceiling that seemed higher and more distant than the sky.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if I’d been shut inside a gigantic box.
hunks.sol: It felt as though I’d been shut inside a gigantic box.

hunks.baseline: But strangely, I wasn’t afraid.
hunks.sol: Strangely, though, I wasn’t afraid.

hunks.baseline: This empty, infinite space was enough to stir some unknowable awe just by looking at it.
hunks.sol: For all its emptiness, the infinite space inspired an awe I couldn’t explain just by looking at it.

hunks.baseline: That’s right.
hunks.sol: Yes.

hunks.baseline: Though it looked nothing like I’d imagined.
hunks.sol: Even if this looked nothing like I’d imagined.

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. That can happen.”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. I suppose so.”

hunks.baseline: A voice came from behind me without any hint of someone’s presence. I instinctively twisted away and retreated, fixing my gaze on the uninvited guest standing only a few steps away.
hunks.sol: A voice came from behind me without any warning. I twisted away on instinct and backed off, keeping my eyes on the uninvited guest standing only a few steps away.

hunks.baseline: “……You’re—”
hunks.sol: “…You’re—”

hunks.baseline: I had no time to be surprised by the new discovery that I could speak.
hunks.sol: I had no time to marvel at the fact that I could speak.

hunks.baseline: The unexpected visitor—or rather, the old man—was a far greater shock.
hunks.sol: The unexpected visitor—an old man—was far more shocking.

hunks.baseline: Unlike me, the old man spoke calmly.
hunks.sol: He, on the other hand, sounded perfectly calm.

hunks.baseline: I nodded and answered as evenly as I could.
hunks.sol: I nodded and tried to answer evenly.

hunks.baseline: “But it’s pretty important to me.”
hunks.sol: “It’s pretty important to me.”

hunks.baseline: “……Who knows?”
hunks.sol: “…Who knows?”

hunks.baseline: I’d sometimes wondered if every enemy I’d defeated really deserved to die like that.
hunks.sol: I’d sometimes wondered whether every enemy I’d defeated had really deserved to die like that.

hunks.baseline: If the pile of corpses and river of blood I’d built with these two hands could be balanced out by the lives of the people who’d survived because of me.
hunks.sol: Whether the mountain of corpses and river of blood I’d made with my own hands could be weighed against all the lives saved because of me.

hunks.baseline: *Maybe I’m the one who deserves to go to hell more than anyone.*
hunks.sol: *Maybe I deserve to go to hell more than anyone.*

hunks.baseline: That was when—
hunks.sol: That was when he spoke.

hunks.baseline: “You’re worrying over nothing. It’s not so easy to get into hell.”
hunks.sol: “You’re worrying over nothing. It’s not so easy to end up in hell.”

hunks.baseline: The old man’s sunken gaze settled on me.
hunks.sol: The old man’s somber gaze rested on me.

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t that what worries you most? That even after you die, you won’t be able to see them.”
hunks.sol: “Isn’t that what worries you most? That you might die and still never see them again?”

hunks.baseline: For a moment, I couldn’t speak. I stared at him, frozen like a statue, then barely managed to squeeze out a voice.
hunks.sol: For a moment, I couldn’t speak. I stared at him, frozen like a statue, then barely managed to force out the words.

hunks.baseline: “Wait. Is this, by any chance—”
hunks.sol: “Wait. Are you—”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, forgive me. I didn’t mean to let that slip.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, forgive me. I let that slip.”

hunks.baseline: His answer was as good as an admission that I’d guessed right.
hunks.sol: His answer all but confirmed my guess.

hunks.baseline: The old man shrugged at me as I struggled to find the words.
hunks.sol: As I struggled to find the words, the old man shrugged.

hunks.baseline: “Well, that’s how it is.”
hunks.sol: “Well, there it is.”

hunks.baseline: “I knew something was off. So it really was true.”
hunks.sol: “I knew something was off. So it really is true.”

hunks.baseline: “It happens more often than you’d think. When the thing you thought couldn’t happen does. It’s easier if you think of it as just one of those cases.”
hunks.sol: “It happens often enough. Sometimes what seems impossible turns out to be real. Think of it as one of those times.”

hunks.baseline: There was no way to make it simple or easy, but for some reason, I could accept it all surprisingly quickly.
hunks.sol: There was nothing simple or comforting about that. Yet, for some reason, I found it surprisingly easy to accept.

hunks.baseline: Even who owned that voice, the one that had sounded like a hallucination just before I opened my eyes in this strange place.
hunks.sol: I even knew who had spoken to me just before I opened my eyes in this strange place.

hunks.baseline: “You’re quick on the uptake. That’s good.”
hunks.sol: “You’re quick on the uptake. Good.”

hunks.baseline: I looked anew at the old man, who now read my thoughts as naturally as breathing.
hunks.sol: I took another look at the old man, who now read my thoughts as naturally as breathing.

hunks.baseline: A spotless robe, not a speck of dust on it. A beard grown so long it reached the floor.
hunks.sol: A robe without a speck of dust on it. A beard long enough to reach the floor.

hunks.baseline: And, for some reason, a feeling of familiarity.
hunks.sol: And something about him that felt oddly familiar.

hunks.baseline: “Have we…… met before?”
hunks.sol: “Have we… met before?”

hunks.baseline: The old man seemed to ponder the question for a while before answering.
hunks.sol: The old man thought for a moment before answering.

hunks.baseline: “We may have. Or we may not have.”
hunks.sol: “We may have. Or we may not.”

hunks.baseline: “This is the best answer I can give you. I have my own circumstances, you see. I’ve already pushed myself quite far to help you.”
hunks.sol: “That’s the best answer I can give. I have my own circumstances to consider. I’ve already gone quite far out of my way to help you.”

hunks.baseline: “Find the answer to that question yourself. You don’t have as much time as you think, so…… let’s get started.”
hunks.sol: “Find the answer to that yourself. We have less time than you might think, so… let’s begin.”

hunks.baseline: I wanted to ask the old man what on earth he was talking about, and what he meant by getting started.
hunks.sol: I wanted to ask what on earth he was talking about, and what he meant by *begin*.

hunks.baseline: But the instant the old man’s figure blurred, it was enough to wipe all the tangled thoughts from my mind.
hunks.sol: But the instant his figure blurred, every tangled thought in my head vanished.

hunks.baseline: Pop.
hunks.sol: *Pop.*

hunks.baseline: I didn’t see him move. I didn’t even feel it.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t seen him move. I hadn’t even sensed it.

hunks.baseline: He was fast enough to leave no afterimage.
hunks.sol: He was so fast he left no afterimage.

hunks.baseline: By the time I turned around, the old man had crossed the few steps between us and gotten behind me. His punch was already filling my vision with black.
hunks.sol: By the time I turned, he had crossed the few steps between us and taken position behind me. His fist blotted out my vision.

hunks.baseline: Thud!
hunks.sol: *Thud!*

hunks.baseline: My vision swam, and strength left my legs.
hunks.sol: My head swam, and my legs went weak.

hunks.baseline: I’d never seen an attack so fast and precise.
hunks.sol: I’d never faced an attack so fast or so precise.

hunks.baseline: But even though I had no reason to fight anymore, I forced my buckling legs to hold and reached out on instinct.
hunks.sol: I had no reason to fight anymore. Even so, I forced my buckling legs to hold and reached out on instinct.

hunks.baseline: Whoosh—BOOM!
hunks.sol: *Whoosh—BOOM!*

hunks.baseline: Before I could even wonder why I still had internal energy, the old man’s characteristically calm voice rang out from beyond the scorching heat.
hunks.sol: Before I could even think about why I had internal energy here, the old man’s calm voice rang out from beyond the scorching heat.

hunks.baseline: “……How do you know that?”
hunks.sol: “…How do you know that?”

hunks.baseline: Whooosh.
hunks.sol: *Whoosh.*

hunks.baseline: The flames split as he answered.
hunks.sol: The flames parted as he answered.

hunks.baseline: Without even forming Palm Force, the old man waved a hand and blew away the heat of the Flame Divine Palm as if snuffing out a candle. Then he signaled to me with his eyes.
hunks.sol: Without even forming Palm Force, the old man swept the heat of the Flame Divine Palm away with a gesture, as though blowing out a candle. Then he glanced at me.

hunks.baseline: “Now, fight back all you like. The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist would do, or the Blazing Flame Divine Spear would be even better.”
hunks.sol: “Go on. Struggle all you like. Try the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist—or better yet, the Blazing Flame Divine Spear.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, but leave out One Annihilation. For your sake, not mine.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, but not One Annihilation. For your sake, not mine.”

hunks.baseline: I could only stare at the ghost—or rather, the old man—in a daze, unable to speak.
hunks.sol: I could only stare at the ghost—or rather, the old man—without a word.

hunks.baseline: Of course, the old man didn’t even allow me that moment.
hunks.sol: Of course, he didn’t even allow me that moment.

hunks.baseline: Slash!
hunks.sol: *Slash!*

hunks.baseline: The old man, who’d been standing amid the dying flames, had already slipped into my blind spot. The invisible qi in the edge of his hand swept smoothly across my chest.
hunks.sol: He’d been standing amid the dying flames, but now he was in my blind spot. Invisible qi carried on the edge of his hand swept smoothly across my chest.

hunks.baseline: So sharp that a beat later, the flesh it sliced through—like tofu—let out a scream.
hunks.sol: It cut through flesh like tofu, so sharply that the pain came a beat later.
*Splurt!*

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed into the air. At the same time, a distant pain I’d thought I’d never feel again came surging back.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed into the air. At the same time, a dizzying pain I’d thought I would never feel again surged through me.

hunks.baseline: Along with the fear I’d briefly forgotten.
hunks.sol: So did the fear I’d briefly forgotten.

hunks.baseline: *At this rate…… I’ll die.*
hunks.sol: *At this rate… I’ll die.*

hunks.baseline: I’d already died once, and yet here I was, thinking about dying again.
hunks.sol: I’d already died once, yet here I was thinking about dying again.

hunks.baseline: But I had no time for questions like that.
hunks.sol: But I had no time to question it.

hunks.baseline: I had to fight back with everything I had against that overwhelming power, powerful enough to erase not just my body but my soul.
hunks.sol: Against a power that seemed capable of erasing not just my body but my soul, I had to struggle with everything I had.

hunks.baseline: The old man nodded, seeing right through my thoughts. A curse slipped out before I could stop it.
hunks.sol: The old man nodded, seeing straight through my thoughts. A curse escaped before I could stop it.

hunks.baseline: “What…… the hell are you?”
hunks.sol: “What… the hell are you?”

hunks.baseline: The old man smiled faintly for the first time. Then he reached out toward me, leaving me speechless at the unexpected family insult.
hunks.sol: The old man smiled faintly for the first time. While I stood speechless at the unexpected family insult, he reached toward me.

hunks.baseline: No—more precisely, he held something out.
hunks.sol: No—he held something out.

hunks.baseline: A spear that had suddenly appeared in midair.
hunks.sol: A spear that had appeared from nowhere.

hunks.baseline: “Take it. Even if you’re going to die, you should at least get to fight back properly once, shouldn’t you?”
hunks.sol: “Take it. If you’re going to die, you might as well put up a proper fight first.”
I gritted my teeth.

hunks.baseline: Gritting my teeth, I grabbed the shaft as the spear flew slowly across the space toward me.
hunks.sol: Then I caught the shaft as the spear flew slowly toward me and spat out the words.

hunks.baseline: Then I spoke through clenched teeth.
The old man replied:
“May you be reborn in paradise.”
hunks.sol: The old man replied, “May you be reborn in paradise.”

hunks.baseline: Ssshh!
hunks.sol: *Shhhk!*
